chapter: Ellington, singers, the book and closing
title: What the book left out: gangsters, the police and ballroom dancing
summary: Mingus says police and gangsters killed big bands and dancing because dancing caused integration; Half Note harassment.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I'm not surprised. Of what was left out of the book as it came out, what do you think was the most important part? That is, what would you most have liked to see in that book?
The gangsters, how they influenced jazz.

And the police, how they stopped the union, how they stopped big band music and started to just focussing on concerts and, like, stop the people from dancing. That was good money for the -- there was a lot of money in those days, when big bands had a place to play.
Now they got these pitty-patty-patty-patty bands.
That nobody hardly goes anymore. They killed the dance floor business.
I know, I hadn't heard the theory before, but --
Well, Joe Jones was the one told me. Old Joe Jones.
He said they stopped the big bands from playing in the ballrooms, because it caused integration.
That I can believe. Because I remember when I first came to New York in the early '50s the cops were really rough on the jazz clubs, where there was an integrated audience.
That's the one I was thinking about.
They would take the soap out of the men's room and then hit them with a complaint.
